exact_statement: Let V(f)=sum_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2 log2(sum_{T containing S} fhat(T)^2/fhat(S)^2), and GV(f) its sum of parent-minus-mean-child increments over physical coordinates. Let b(x)=g(x0,x1,x2)g(x3,x4,x5), with g=-1 only at000, delta=1/64, a_n balanced majority on n=2m+1 controls, m>=1, and F_n=b*a_n at data points0,e0, b elsewhere. For h_n(y,z)=(-1)^y a_n(z), GV(F_n)-2delta GV(h_n)>=delta log2(m+1)-37, whereas I_DATA(F_n)<=6. Therefore no finite constant K>=0 makes GV(F_n)<=2delta GV(h_n)+K I_DATA(F_n) hold for all m. The root marked-singleton term J_y(h_n) is zero, so a fixed root J credit cannot fix this. In contrast -37<=GV(F_n)-2delta GV(a_n)<=49 and I_DATA(F_n)>=21/16; the original-controller transfer holds with K=256 for this same family. An explicit failure of the unmarked-selector K=256 transfer is m=2^100736. These statements concern a proposed potential-transfer inequality, not unbounded Fourier H/I. Moreover, for the SAME fixed seed and pair of adjacent edits, EVERY balanced Boolean controller a on ANY finite number of uniform control bits obeys GV(F)-2delta GV(a)<70 and I_DATA(F)>=21/16, hence GV(F)<=2delta GV(a)+256 I_DATA(F). The two edits use the SAME controller; two different dependent controllers are not covered.
